source: UAE Federal Customs Authority, Dubai Customs, Abu Dhabi Customs

prohibited_items.reason: Strictly prohibited under UAE Federal Law. Zero tolerance policy. Severe penalties including imprisonment.
Prohibited for import into UAE. Not allowed through customs.
Illegal in the UAE. All electronic devices may be checked.
Regulated in UAE. Can be purchased locally but importing may require declaration.
BANNED in UAE. Codeine is classified as a controlled narcotic substance. Common Indian cough syrups like Corex and Phensedyl contain codeine.

restricted_items.reason: Allowed with valid prescription and doctor's letter. Some medicines legal in India are BANNED in UAE (e.g., codeine, some painkillers). Maximum 3-month supply.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: Doctor's prescription, medical certificate, medicine list attested by hospital. Check specific medicine on UAE MOH website.

restricted_items.reason: Controlled substances in UAE. Require special approval from UAE Ministry of Health BEFORE travel.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: Prior approval from UAE MOH, original prescription, doctor's letter stating condition and dosage.

restricted_items.reason: Non-Muslim travelers over 21 can bring limited alcohol through duty-free (varies by emirate). Dubai: 4 liters or equivalent. Abu Dhabi: 2 liters.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: Must be purchased from duty-free only. Must be 21+ years old.
restricted_items.official_source: Dubai Duty Free / Abu Dhabi Customs

restricted_items.reason: Allowed up to 400 cigarettes or 500g tobacco per person. Gutka and pan masala with tobacco are BANNED.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: None for allowed quantities. Excess subject to duty.

restricted_items.reason: Personal food items generally allowed in reasonable quantities. Dried fish and meat products may be inspected. Must be properly packed and sealed.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: None for personal use quantities. Commercial quantities need import permit.

restricted_items.reason: Personal electronics are allowed. Drones require registration with UAE GCAA. Satellite phones are banned.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: Drones: GCAA registration. Satellite phones: Not allowed.

restricted_items.reason: Personal jewelry is allowed. Large quantities may need to be declared. Carrying gold bars/coins above the limit requires customs declaration.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: Declaration form if exceeding personal use quantity. Keep purchase receipts.

restricted_items.reason: Official UAE Federal Customs Authority (FCA) limit: Any traveler (18+) carrying cash, currencies, bearer negotiable instruments, or precious metals/stones exceeding AED 60,000 (or equivalent in foreign currency, approx. ₹13.5 Lakhs) MUST declare it via the Afsah customs app or at airport declaration counters upon arrival. Failure to declare leads to confiscation and legal penalties.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: UAE Customs 'Afsah' declaration form or declaration counter at customs if exceeding AED 60,000.
restricted_items.official_source: UAE Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security (FCA - fca.gov.ae)

restricted_items.reason: Over-the-counter pain reliever. Allowed for personal use in reasonable quantities.
restricted_items.paperwork_needed: None for personal use. Carry in original packaging.

general_advice: Always carry medicines in original packaging with labels
Keep a doctor's prescription for all prescription medicines
Declare any items you're unsure about at customs – penalties for non-declaration are severe
Check the UAE MOH website for the latest list of controlled medicines before travel
When in doubt, contact the UAE Embassy or customs authority before packing the item
